channel.title: The Daily Digest
channel.description: One top story from each of my chosen publications, updated daily.

item.title: NYT: Tech Stocks Tumble, but Broader Market Is Holding On
item.description: The S&P 500 is set for a small loss for the month, despite a deeper slide in some of the A.I. stocks that exert a heavy influence on the index.

item.title: NPR: NPR special: 5 takeaways from a year of listening to swing voters
item.description: Every election, there is a crucial sliver of voters who help determine which candidates win. Here are five takeaways from a year of listening to voters who backed Biden in 2020 and then Trump in 2024.

item.title: BBC News: What we know about Binance's $6.3bn hack
item.description: Cyber correspondent Joe Tidy explains more about what is suspected to be the biggest hack in history.

item.title: The Guardian: Reader Q&A: How can we radically change the way we live? Ask Aditya Chakrabortty
item.description: Guardian columnist, senior economics commentator and host of the new Radical Thinking podcast Aditya Chakrabortty is answering your questions on the big ideas around economics, society and democracy, and his new podcast…

item.title: Al Jazeera: Jerusalem Daily: Israel’s siege on Hebron displaces thousands
item.description: Israel has announced its final election results, tightened its siege on Hebron, and arrested people returning to Gaza.

item.title: Ars Technica: GM to pay $220 million after selling customer Smart Driver data
item.description: Owners of GM cars found their driving data had been sold to insurance companies.

item.title: WIRED Backchannel: I Gave My Blood to the AI Death Clock
item.description: Death Clock promises to predict when you’re going to die and help you extend your time on Earth. After a month, I felt like it was sucking the life out of me.

item.title: WIRED Science: Crematoria Are Being Used to Heat Homes and Swimming Pools
item.description: European countries are leading the way harvesting heat that would otherwise be wasted as green death practices become more common.

item.title: WIRED Business: I Spent 30 Minutes With Apple’s CEO. Now I Know Why John Ternus Got the Job
item.description: Apple doesn’t need fixing, and it doesn’t want drama. Its new leader is a “product guy” who bleeds six colors.

item.title: The New Yorker: The Real Stakes of the Ilhan Omar Case
item.description: In seeking to revoke the citizenship of a sitting congresswoman, the Trump Administration has sent a chilling message about dissent, loyalty, and who gets to be an American.

item.title: New York Mag The Cut: ‘I Am a Bad Roommate’
item.description: How the housemates from hell justify their crimes against communal living.

item.title: New York Mag Curbed: What Is John Turturro’s NYQ?
item.description: On a scale from a pocket park to The Only Living Pickpocket in New York, where does the Severance actor fit?

item.title: Fox59: IMPD: Man killed in shooting on northeast side
item.description: INDIANAPOLIS – A man died following an early Friday morning shooting on the northeast side. According to the Indianapolis Metropolitan Police Department, officers were dispatched around 2:20 a.m. Friday to Ellis and Shad…
